settings.title: Feeds
settings.direct: Vedette fetches each feed directly from its source. Some sources publish their lists on GitHub, so those come from raw.githubusercontent.com; Vedette's own GitHub repository is used only for software updates.

builtin.title: Built-in feeds
builtin.description: Turn a feed off, change how often it is fetched, or point it at a mirror you host. Built-in feeds cannot be deleted.
builtin.caption: Built-in feeds

custom.title: Your own feeds
custom.description: Add a feed from your company or a partner: vulnerabilities, or indicators of compromise (IOC). You decide how Vedette reads it.
custom.caption: Your own feeds
custom.vulnNote: A vulnerability feed of your own is shown on CVE pages and in lookups. It does not create findings or alerts: only the CISA list is matched against your devices.
custom.empty: No feeds of your own yet
custom.emptyBody: Add a vulnerability feed or an IOC list, tell Vedette how to read it, and preview the result before saving.

hosts.title: Where this box connects
hosts.description: Every address the box pulls feeds from, built-in and your own, read from the list above. Only your IP address reaches them; none of your data is sent.
hosts.cisaMirror: (and raw.githubusercontent.com if www.cisa.gov does not answer)

row.firstFetch: Fetched at the next scheduled check (every 5 minutes), or now with Fetch now.

dialog.mirrorHint: Use a mirror if you host a copy of this feed yourself. https only, except addresses on your network.
dialog.builtinBody: The schedule and address Vedette uses to fetch this feed.
dialog.customBody: Vedette fetches this feed directly from its address on the schedule you choose.
dialog.name: Name

typeHint.ioc: Indicators: IP address, domain, URL or file hash, with confidence and first seen.
typeHint.vulnerabilities: CVE, vendor, product, date, description and link. Shown on CVE pages and in lookups, but it never creates findings or alerts: only the CISA list is matched against your devices.

dialog.urlHint: https only, except addresses on your network (private ranges, .local). Vedette never pulls a feed from itself.
dialog.secretHint: At least 8 characters. Stored encrypted; only the last 4 characters are shown afterwards.

err.name: Enter a name.
err.url: Enter a full address such as https://example.com/feed.json.
err.https: Use an https:// address. http:// is only allowed for internal addresses.
err.blocked: Vedette does not pull feeds from link-local, multicast, unspecified or cloud metadata addresses.
err.own: That address is Vedette itself: loopback, Vedette's own container, or one of its ports (8443, 8444, 8765, 514, 6514) on the machine that runs it. For another program on that machine, enter the machine's LAN address and that program's port.
err.header: Enter a header name such as X-Api-Key.
err.secretShape: The secret must be at least 8 characters with no spaces.

parser.title: How Vedette reads this feed
parser.intro: Choose the format, say where each field is, then test on a sample. Rows that do not fit are counted and skipped, never crash the fetch.

recordsHint.vulnerabilities: JSONPath to the list of records, for example $.vulnerabilities[*]. Supported: .key, ['key'], [n], [*].
recordsHint.ioc: JSONPath to the list of records, for example $.data[*] or $.indicators[*]. Supported: .key, ['key'], [n], [*].

note.json: Each record is mapped with a JSONPath relative to it, such as {{example}}.
note.csv: Lines starting with # are skipped. Name a column from the header, or give its number.
note.rss: Use item fields: title, link, description, pubDate (or published), category, id.
note.stix: Vedette reads indicator objects and their patterns, such as [ipv4-addr:value = '203.0.113.7'], [domain-name:value = '...'], [url:value = '...'] and file hashes. A bundle or a TAXII collection response both work. Fields are fixed; nothing to map.
note.lines: One indicator per line; blank lines and # comments are skipped. Only the first word on each line is used. The kind (IP, domain, URL, hash) is detected.

parser.srcJson: JSONPath, for example {{example}}. Empty = not mapped.
parser.srcCsv: Column name or number. Empty = not mapped.
parser.regexHint: The first capture group is kept; no match rejects the row.
parser.ownPlaceholder: Paste a few lines of the feed here
parser.ownHint: Leave empty to use a built-in sample of this format.
parser.limits: Limits: {{size}} MB and {{rows}} rows per fetch.
parser.truncated: Stopped at the row limit ({{rows}}). Remaining rows would be ignored.
parser.noRecords: No records came out. Check the paths, column names or regex.
parser.firstRejectedLines: First rejected lines of the sample
